title: Internal Hom preserves finite Tor amplitude by dévissage
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $A$ a
finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring, and $X$ a scheme of finite type over
$k$. For $K,L\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$, the internal Hom
$R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$ lies in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$.

Here $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ denotes the full subcategory of the ordinary derived category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ on the small étale site consisting of bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in some interval $[a,b]$, $a\leq b$, against every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. The internal Hom is the ambient derived internal Hom of the ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No separatedness assumption on $X$ or presentation of $A$ as a quotient of a discrete valuation ring is imposed.

proof.text: Convert the two hypotheses and the desired conclusion between finite-value bounded constructibility with an ordered Tor interval and the source constructibleFiniteTor predicate. In each degree use lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison. Cohomology vanishing is equivalent to the IsGE and IsLE conditions. In the reverse direction replace each possibly reversed interval [a,b] by [min a b,max a b]. The private devissage_ctf_iff proves both directions, including zero objects and empty schemes.

Let Ω be the algebraic closure of k. By lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep, Ω/k is purely inseparable. The instance Algebra.IsUniversalHomeomorphism.of_isPurelyInseparable (lem-pc-spec-pure-insep-integral-radicial-surjective) makes Spec Ω → Spec k a universal homeomorphism, and base change gives one f:Y = X ×_k Ω → X. The map Y → Spec Ω is still of finite type. Pullback carries both inputs to constructibleFiniteTor by the proved source theorem constructibleFiniteTor_mapDerivedCategory_upperStar. If ℓ^n vanishes in A, then ℓ^n is a positive annihilator invertible in k and hence on Y; this supplies HasInvertibleExponent A Y, without any nonzero-ring assumption.

source.place: constructibleFiniteTor_mapDerivedCategory_upperStar; Mathlib base-change instances for locally finite type and quasi-compact morphisms

proof.text: Apply the existing source-library boundedConstructible_derivedHom and torAmplitudeIn_derivedHom over Ω. These declarations accept any finite commutative coefficient ring with invertible exponent, not only the special coefficient presentations of the Sheaf.Paper wrappers. They require algebraic closedness, now available for Ω, and finite type, without separatedness. The source exists_topologicalKrullDim_le supplies the natural dimension bound for the Tor theorem. Together their conclusions give constructibleFiniteTor for RHom(f* K,f* L). This reuses the already-written source proof rather than asserting a new preservation lemma.

By prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos the exact monoidal sheaf pullback F=f* is an equivalence. Let E be its derived equivalence, H=RHom(EK,EL), Q=E.inverse(H). The counit identifies E(Q) with H. Bounded constructibility descends by boundedConstructible_of_upperStar_of_isUniversalHomeomorphism and Tor amplitude reflects by DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_of_mapDerivedCategory. Thus Q is constructibleFiniteTor. The units K ≅ E.inverse(EK), L ≅ E.inverse(EL), contravariance/covariance of RHom, and DerivedCategory.ihomCompMapDerivedCategoryInvIso give RHom(K,L) ≅ Q. Transfer membership along this isomorphism and use Step 1. The private devissage_hom_equivalence performs only this comparison with abstract coefficients to keep the kernel check of the derived monoidal instances small; devissage_hom_descends specializes it and carries out the reflection.
